The cooper's child. Small. To the narrow galleries. Restless. Rebind weekly.

Remarks: the yard is the finest source in Skyrim. The dead of Falkreath are many and their families visit seldom. With forty more I can finish opening the lower vault, and what lies under it was old when Arkay was new. I do not intend to share it with the cell in the Reach. Corvus is not to know of this page.

notes.title: Apprentice's Diary
notes.author: Hesta
pages:
#Sun's Dusk
Mistress Velmira has me mending the bindings on the little one. She keeps walking north toward Falkreath. I asked the Mistress why we do not let her go, since she is so small and so much trouble. The Mistress looked at me for a long while and I have not asked anything since.

#Later
I found the little one's name scratched on the wall of her alcove, in her own hand, I think, from before. Sigrid. I have started calling her that. She stopped walking north for a whole day. If the Mistress finds out I will be in the kitchen with the widow.

notes.title: Defaced Altar of Arkay
pages:
The old altar at the heart of the sanctum still bears its blessing, carved by Arkay's priests long ago:
'Here the dead rest in the circle of birth and death, and none shall break it.'
Across the words someone has daubed, in dark paint: 'Circles are made to be broken.' The paint is flaking. The carving underneath is not.

At the foot of the altar, scratched into the stone floor in a child's uneven letters: SIGRID. And beside it, smaller, in an adult's neat hand: 'I am sorry. - H.' Somebody has left a dried flower on the name, the only clean thing in the room.

bloodlet_throne.hook: A grim fortress on the high pass south of Falkreath, held by a vampire court that takes its tithe in blood from the travellers of the Pale Pass road.
bloodlet_throne.rumour: Bloodlet Throne. They don't rob you, the ones up there. They count you. They count everyone who uses that road, and every so often, the count comes up short.

notes.title: The Red Tithe
notes.author: Lady Arnvor of the Throne
pages:
Tithe for the season of Hearthfire, taken from the Pale Pass road:
One carter of Helgen, a refugee, fed upon.
Two pilgrims bound for the Ancestor Glade, kept.
One Legion courier, kept. His dispatches burned unread.
The miller's boy from the Half-Moon road, fed upon and returned, for kindness costs little and buys silence.

To the master of Haemar's Shame: our offer stands. You have the Rift's thin, sour blood. We have Falkreath's, sweet with pine and grief. Trade with us, or do not. But do not lecture us about the Dawnguard. The Dawnguard is far away, and we are very old.

notes.title: Letter Written in Charcoal
notes.author: Hallvard the pilgrim
pages:
Wife,
We never reached the glade. They took us on the road below the fortress, at dusk, with no more noise than wind. There are perhaps a dozen of them. The one they call Lady Arnvor is the oldest, and she likes to talk. She has asked me what I miss most, three nights running, and written down my answers.

If this reaches Falkreath, give it to Bailiff Eirik. Tell him the cells are under the great hall, and that the creatures sleep in the eastern tower from dawn until the sun is well down. Tell him to come by day. Tell our son I was not afraid. That is a lie. Tell him anyway.

notes.title: Decree of the Throne
pages:
By the will of Lady Arnvor:
No kill on the road within sight of Falkreath's walls. The town must think it is wolves.
No kill of Legion soldiers by more than one in a season. The Legion counts.
The Stormcloaks may pass freely. They are good for the war, and the war is good for us: graves are dug faster than anyone can watch them.

Postscript, in the same elegant hand: 'The Lady reminds her court that the Dawnguard has a fort in the Rift and long memories. Let Haemar's Shame take their attention. We are patient. We will outlast the war, the Dawnguard, and the Empire, if we are careful with our appetites.'

the_lady_stone.hook: An ancient standing stone on a small island in Lake Ilinalta, blessed by the Lady sign. Pilgrims row out to it for healing, and the millfolk of Half-Moon leave wreaths.
the_lady_stone.rumour: Brynja rows out to the Lady Stone every spring with a wreath for her mother. Says her mother lost something in the shallows there on her wedding day and never got it back.

notes.title: Verse on the Stone's Base
pages:
Carved around the foot of the stone, in old runes worn soft by the lake wind:
'The Lady keeps the mended and the mending. Rest here, and rise whole.'
Newer letters have been cut beside them by a less practised hand: 'Ingrun and Ottar, wed here on the 9th of Second Seed. She dropped her comb in the water. He said he'd find it. He never did. He said he'd find it every year after. Love, Brynja.'

On the far side of the stone, someone has cut a tally of short lines in groups of five, thirty in all. The most recent are deeper and more careful than the rest, as if made by an old man who had to rest between each one.

notes.title: Pilgrim's Prayer
pages:
~Lady of the lake stone, mend what I broke,
~The bone and the promise, the word that I spoke,
~Make whole what is torn, make warm what is cold,
~And keep me, when weary, from growing too old.

A slip of paper tucked into a crack in the stone, weighted with a pebble.
The paper is signed only with a small drawing of a crutch. Beneath the pebble that weights it lies another, and beneath that another: a little cairn of pebbles, one for every pilgrim who came here limping and rowed home without needing to.

the_guardian_stones.hook: Three ancient standing stones on the road between Riverwood and Helgen, each marked with a constellation: the Warrior, the Mage and the Thief. Every traveller is said to be drawn to one.
the_guardian_stones.rumour: Everyone who walks past the Guardian Stones feels one of them pulling. Mine was the Thief. My wife says that explains a great deal.

notes.title: A Wayfarer's Carving
pages:
Scratched into the flat rock between the three stones by some long-gone traveller:
'The Warrior asked me what I would fight for. The Mage asked me what I would learn. The Thief asked me what I would take. I could not answer all three, so I chose the one that asked the question I was afraid of.'
Below it, in a different hand: 'Which one was that?' And below that, in the first hand again: 'Go and find out.'

Travellers have added to the carving over the years. One has scratched a sword, one a book, one a key. Someone has scratched all three and written beside them: 'Greedy.' Another has answered: 'Prepared.'

notes.title: Note Left Under a Stone
pages:
Buyer,
Next load from Embershard will be at the stones on Middas, at dusk, ground clean of the mark. Bring the usual and not a copper less, Skarn says the price of iron's gone up since the war. Stand by the Thief stone, it's the one in the shadow. Don't bring Riverwood folk. Don't bring anybody.

Last load short by two sacks. Skarn says that's on you, not us, since you counted it in the dark. Bring a lantern this time. But keep it hooded till you're past the stones, the Riverwood guards walk the road on Middas now. If they stop you, you're a pilgrim. You've come to pray to the Thief. It's not even a lie.

word_wall_lost_valley_redoubt.hook: An ancient Word Wall above the falls of Lost Valley Redoubt, its dragon script carved deep into the cliff. Hagravens and Forsworn guard the valley below.
word_wall_lost_valley_redoubt.rumour: There's a wall of dragon writing up past Bilegulch, over the Lost Valley falls. The Forsworn hold the valley, and the hagravens make their prayers to that wall like it might answer.

notes.title: Rubbing from the Lost Valley Wall
notes.author: Calvus Aterius, antiquarian
pages: Charcoal rubbing of the central panel, with my notes. The script is the same as on the Bilegulch and Sunderstone mounds, which supports my view that all three were made by one dragon cult. One word recurs, carved deeper than the rest and in a separate hand, as if added in haste. The local Forsworn call it 'the word that walks through walls'.

I copied it twice. Each time, my hand passed through the paper for a moment, as though the paper had become smoke. I have decided not to copy it a third time. Further work on the mound below Bilegulch is assigned to my assistant, Ennis.

dragon_mound_bilegulch_mine.hook: A burial mound of the Dragon War on the slopes above Bilegulch Mine, split open from within. Draugr have been seen walking around it at dusk, as though on guard.
dragon_mound_bilegulch_mine.rumour: The orcs at Bilegulch say the old mound up the hill cracked open one night with a sound like a mountain coughing. Now there's dead men standing around it, waiting.

notes.title: Ennis Hollowgate's Field Journal
notes.author: Ennis Hollowgate, assistant to Calvus Aterius
pages:
#27th of Hearthfire
Arrived at the Bilegulch mound. The stone cap is thrown outward, not dug inward; Master Calvus was right. The bones in the pit are gone. Scorch marks on the rim, as though something breathed fire on its way out.

#28th of Hearthfire
Three draugr walk the rim at dusk. They do not attack. They watch the sky. I think they are waiting for their master to return. I have hidden my satchel with the survey drawings in the rocks by the pit and will go down to the orcs for help. Should have gone yesterday.

dragon_mound_evergreen_grove.hook: An ancient dragon burial mound in the pines near Evergreen Grove, its stone broken open from below. The spriggans of the grove will not go near it.
dragon_mound_evergreen_grove.rumour: Even the spriggans keep clear of that mound by the grove. Calvus at the inn pays a septim for every rumour about it. I've given him four. Three were true.

notes.title: Survey Notes, Mound the First
notes.author: Calvus Aterius, antiquarian
pages:
The Evergreen mound. Cap stone shattered outward. Burial pit empty to the bedrock. The surrounding pines are scorched on the side facing the pit but green on the far side, indicating a blast of heat from within (1).
(1) My colleagues in Cyrodiil will say I am credulous. My colleagues in Cyrodiil have not stood here.

This makes the third open mound in Falkreath Hold. I intend to compare the Evergreen mound to those near Sunderstone Gorge and Bilegulch Mine. If all three opened in the same season, then something is going from mound to mound, waking what lies inside. The local word for it is dragon. I have stopped laughing at the local word.

dragon_mound_sunderstone_gorge.hook: A Dragon War burial mound on the high ground north of Sunderstone Gorge, its pit empty and its rim blackened. Scholars come, measure it, and leave in a hurry.
dragon_mound_sunderstone_gorge.rumour: Somebody's been camping by the old mound north of Sunderstone. Breton fellow, ink on his fingers. Haven't seen him in a while. Hope he moved on.

notes.title: Measurements in a Neat Hand
notes.author: Ennis Hollowgate
pages: Sunderstone mound. Diameter of pit: nineteen paces. Depth: four men. Cap stone thrown thirty paces to the northeast. Same pattern as Evergreen. The skeleton is gone and so are the grave goods, if there were any.

Master Calvus wants Bilegulch done by the end of the month. It is a day's walk west, past the orc mine, and the orcs throw rocks at anyone who comes near. I have bought a jar of honey to give them. I am told Orcs like honey. I am told a great many things.

dragon_mound_greywater_grotto.hook: A dragon burial mound in the southern hills below Greywater Grotto, torn open from within. The shepherds who saw it happen still will not speak of the night.
dragon_mound_greywater_grotto.rumour: A shepherd south of Helgen saw that mound open. Said the ground shook, the stone flew, and something rose out of it and flew south toward Ancient's Ascent. He doesn't keep sheep anymore.

notes.title: A Shepherd's Account
notes.author: Taken down by the Falkreath steward's clerk
pages:
Account of Arnulf, shepherd, given at the Jarl's longhouse.
He states that on the night of the 2nd of Hearthfire a great black dragon flew low over his pasture and circled the old mound below Greywater Grotto. It spoke words that shook the stones. The mound split, and from it rose a second, smaller beast, dun-coloured and stinking of old earth.

The black one flew north. The dun one flew south and settled on Ancient's Ascent, where it has stayed. The shepherd requests the hold compensate him for eleven sheep. The steward has noted that the hold does not compensate for dragons. The shepherd has noted that he would like to see the steward tell the dragon that.
